issues.reason: The preposition-named oblique is defined as a binary relation on an event or entity symbol ((<Prep> <event> <object>), entity-attached (From sk_wool_1 calderwick)), and Core patterns enumerates the sealing carriers as attitudes/embedded questions/directives/counterfactuals/AccordingTo, so nesting an (And ...) proposition in In's first slot is ill-typed per the vocabulary.

Conditional properties states that a locative or domain PP restricting a kind-level claim goes in the condition slot ((ConditionalProperty rent steep sk_capital_1)), which is exactly this construction (a domain PP over the kind-level claim about salt), and the parse uses a different carrier.

The misattachment half stands — the argument-PP doctrine puts a noun's complement on that noun's OWN symbol, so (For substitute sea_water) records a claim about substitutes at large rather than about salt — but the prescriptive half is overstated: the fuse-into-one-property route (sensitive_to_light) is stated for an ADJECTIVE with a bare-kind complement, as the reviewer's own gap concedes.

Compound decomposition requires the head genus unconditionally ('always emit the genus', hyphenated/solid spellings included), and the seal-projection table lists definitional decomposition atoms of compound kinds as projecting, so (Inheritance sea_water water) (STV 1.0 0.99) is missing.

The half that stands is that the strength-0.0 must sit on a licensed kind-level claim atom rather than on an In wrapper, since as written nothing about salt is queryable; the half that is overstated is the prescribed remedy — a bare (Inheritance salt <predicate>) (STV 0.0 ...) would silently drop the 'in distillation' restriction, which Core patterns forbids ('omitting it widens the claim').

gaps_confirmed: a copular clause whose PREDICATE NOMINAL takes a PP complement ('X is a substitute for Y') at kind level: the argument-PP oblique needs the noun's own symbol and the fuse-into-one-property route is stated only for adjectives, so a predicate nominal has no symbol to carry the argument
negating a kind-level claim that also carries a domain/locative restriction: no polarity treatment is stated for the ConditionalProperty condition-slot route
new_gaps: two carriers collide for a domain PP over a kind-level claim: 'Where a THING is' routes a framing/domain PP to the preposition-named oblique (In <what-is-claimed> fluid_mechanics), while 'Conditional properties' routes a domain PP restricting a kind-level claim to the ConditionalProperty condition slot — the instruction set does not say which wins, nor what fills the oblique's first slot when what-is-claimed is a categorical with no event or entity symbol
defect_summary: Issue 0/1/4: the domain restriction and the negation belong on a licensed kind-level atom — (ConditionalProperty salt <property> distillation) (STV 0.0 0.9) — not on a proposition nested in the In oblique's first slot; issue 2: the 'for sea-water' argument must attach to salt's own predicate symbol, not to the bare class substitute; issue 3: emit (Inheritance sea_water water) (STV 1.0 0.99) at top level. NO fully licensed form exists for the <property> slot: fusing to substitute_for_sea_water with (Inheritance substitute_for_sea_water substitute) + (For substitute_for_sea_water sea_water) is an analogical extension of an adjective-only rule, so the predicate-nominal-with-PP-complement gap above is what a fix would actually require.
notes: The STV 0.0 0.9 choice (negated empirical kind-level claim) is correct and not at issue. Both In and For are licensed heads; the defect is the sealing USE of the oblique plus the complement landing on a bare class symbol.
